A 2024 study evaluated six metamorphic relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise, finding that input/output consistency checks expose recommender reliability defects without requiring exact expected recommendations. This supports testing diagnostic sensitivity before further model changes, but does not establish coverage for BERT4Rec routing or export faults. [Study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410)

BERT4Rec requires family-specific checks: masked-target training prevents bidirectional target leakage; inference appends MASK and reads its representation. RecTools explicitly implements left padding and appended-MASK inference. For this harness, proposed controlled mutations include count-minus-one readout, omitted MASK, disabled padding attention mask, swapped category routing, mismatched checkpoint configuration, and incorrect candidate filtering. Padding-invariance tests must preserve positional semantics; adding padding can change outputs legitimately when absolute position IDs shift. [BERT4Rec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), [RecTools implementation](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/rectools/models/nn/transformers/bert4rec.html)

A practical validation design is to compare the trained module and freshly loaded predictor on identical histories/candidates, with evaluation mode enabled, then inject each fault separately. PyTorch documents state-dictionary loading and the need for `model.eval()` during inference. Report detection coverage over applicable non-equivalent mutants, false-alarm rate on clean controls, and runtime; also test candidate-order equivariance, batch-order equivariance, and category/checkpoint identity. These are proposed checks, not measured results on the current trial. Preserve one trained checkpoint per category and the unchanged host evaluator. [PyTorch saving/loading guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html)
